The main takeaway from our work is that

the North Icelandic Shelf is a highly sensitive region of the North Atlantic that is strongly affected by climate changes in the Arctic and North Atlantic, and the chronology we present here provides an important new tool for investigating these changes in a region of the North Iceland Shelf where proxy archives have been relatively sparse.
A. islandica is a valuable archive of climate variability, and that it can provide an absolutely-dated, long-term perspective on the marine environment of high-latitude shelf seas.

A. islandica can be used to construct a robust, high-resolution, absolutely dated chronology of marine climate on decadal to centennial timescales, and the method can be applied to other regions to provide a more complete picture of the marine environment of past centuries.
